$comment: What a connection failure is called, in words. Read by tests/shared/connectionerror.test.ts and the Android SharedCorpusTest. A failed handshake arrives as whatever the platform's library calls it, and both clients showed that verbatim — accurate, and not English. A certificate that does not match the address is what being intercepted looks like, so it is the one a person most needs to understand.
$cases: `raw` is what the platform said; `problem` is what we make of it.

cases.name: Android says the names do not match
cases.raw: No subjectAltNames on the certificate match

cases.name: and the other way it says it
cases.raw: java.security.cert.CertificateException: No subject alternative DNS name matching irc.example.org found.

cases.name: Node says it its own way
cases.raw: Hostname/IP does not match certificate's altnames: Host: irc.example.org. is not in the cert's altnames

cases.name: Android cannot build a chain
cases.raw: java.security.cert.CertPathValidatorException: Trust anchor for certification path not found.

cases.name: Node has three ways of saying the same
an issuer it has never heard of
an ordinary refusal is left alone
and so is a closed socket

$sentences: And what is shown, for a server called irc.example.org.

sentences.name: a mismatch says so, and says nothing was sent
sentences.text: The certificate irc.example.org presented is for a different address. This may not be the server you meant — nothing was sent.

sentences.name: an untrusted issuer
sentences.text: The certificate irc.example.org presented is signed by an authority this device does not trust. Nothing was sent.

sentences.name: an expired certificate
sentences.text: The certificate irc.example.org presented has expired. Nothing was sent.
